episodes.211834: A weak disturbance moving across the Intermountain West combined with intense daytime heating resulting in scattered high based evaporating showers and dry thunderstorms across western and central New Mexico during the afternoon hours on May 13th. These showers resulted in dry microbursts at the Farmington Four Corners Regional Airport and the NMDOT weather station along I-40 at SR6 in Laguna Pueblo. High based shower and thunderstorm activity across western and central New Mexico dissipated around sunset with the loss of daytime heating. Two rounds of high based shower and thunderstorm activity developed across the eastern plains of New Mexico during the afternoon hours on May 14th and 15th with dry microbursts in Clayton. High based shower and thunderstorm activity exited east into west Texas and tapered off during the evening hours, with one area of collapsing showers resulting in a heat burst at the Fort Sumner Municipal Airport late on May 14th.
episodes.211874: On May 13th, scattered thunderstorms with strong and damaging winds impacted northeast Montana late in the day. After which, a re-enforcing cold front brought additional widespread damaging winds. Recently plowed fields allowed this wind to create areas of blowing dust on the 14th.
episodes.211957: Surface low pressure stationed across southern Ontario gradually shifted eastward throughout the afternoon hours of May 13, 2026. Some showers and thunderstorms forming ahead of a surface cold frontal passage and along the cold front was stationed in an environment of sufficient deep-layer shear along with steepening low- and mid-level lapse rates that brought a marginal wind threat during that afternoon and evening hours. This severe wind threat allowed for scattered instances of tree damage across central Pennsylvania with the most damage across the Lower Susquehanna Valley where slightly better shear and moisture was available during the evening hours.
episodes.212080: A strong cold front moved into an warm and unstable airmass primarily west of I-95. This resulted in bands of showers and thunderstorms that produced localized damaging wind and spotty large hail.
episodes.212081: A strong cold front moved into an warm and unstable airmass primarily west of I-95. This resulted in bands of showers and thunderstorms that produced localized damaging wind and spotty large hail.
episodes.212082: A strong cold front moved into an warm and unstable airmass primarily west of I-95. This resulted in bands of showers and thunderstorms that produced localized damaging wind and spotty large hail.
episodes.212549: A strong cold front, combined with scattered thunderstorms embedded in southwest flow, interacted with an anomalously warm and dry air mass across southwest Montana. High temperatures were in the 80s, creating large dewpoint depressions. High winds aloft, reaching 65 knots between 16,000 and 18,000 feet MSL, were brought to the surface by both convective downdrafts and evaporative cooling, as well as the passing cold front. This synoptic setup led to severe and high wind gusts across the region.
episodes.212667: A trough brought an increase in southerly winds aloft on the 13th. This combined with a strongly unstable atmosphere brought severe thunderstorms producing scattered severe wind gusts across the region. High synoptic wind gusts also accompanied thunderstorms on the 13th and 14th.
episodes.212849: After a morning of showers and overcast clouds on May 13th, clearing skies during the afternoon resulted in strong thunderstorm development across West Virginia. Convection initially developed during the early afternoon west of the Ohio River, then crossed into north-central West Virginia during peak heating hours. This helped to maintain severe strength in some of the storms that crossed through Lewis and Calhoun Counties. Local power outages caused by downed trees and small to large hail were noted in locations north of Route 50, with one lone instance of sub-severe hail taking place in Raleigh County. The broken line of storms tracked east of the forecast area by the evening, bringing the risk for severe weather to an end for the day.
episodes.212868: A grazing shortwave trough north of Utah sent a cold front into the region. Ahead of and along this boundary there was enough moisture to result in isolated to scattered convective development, with much of this activity higher based in nature. As a result, numerous strong to severe wind gusts were recorded or reported. Additionally, a period of strong winds downsloping off of terrain was noted in portions of northwest Utah following the passage of the frontal boundary.
episodes.212871: A cold front moving through the central Appalachian mountains during the peak heating of the afternoon triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms to form. The presence of modest instability allowed a couple of these storms to grow intense enough to produce damaging wind gusts, which resulted in localized damage to trees.
episodes.212872: A cold front moving through the central Appalachian mountains during the peak heating of the afternoon caused scattered showers and thunderstorms to form. The presence of modest instability allowed a couple of these storms produce damaging wind gusts, resulting in a few instances of tree damage.
episodes.213134: A low pressure system moving north of the area brought periods of rain Wednesday morning (13th), followed by scattered showers as a cold front approached. Partial clearing during the afternoon allowed for modest destabilization across western portions of the area. Combined with wind shear and unstable temperature lapse rates, thunderstorms organized along the front as they moved east through the evening. A few storms produced isolated damaging wind gusts and small hail. The strong gusts and small hail resulted in some crop damage according to a state emergency declaration, though estimated costs were unknown.
episodes.213253: A line of storms moved across most of WNY producing sporadic reports of damaging winds.
episodes.213448: Mid-afternoon thunderstorms both in broken line segments and single cells developed along and ahead of a cold front. Marginal effective shear values up to 30 knots and MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg supported severe thunderstorms producing both wind and hail. Wind was primarily confined to northern West Virginia along a DCAPE gradient of 600-700 J/kg. Mid-level lapse rates up to 6.5 C/km and up to 300 J/kg of hail growth zone CAPE supported numerous reports of quarter size within storms across western Pennsylvania.

episodes.213567: A slow moving band of thunderstorms dumped 6-8 inches of rain in a short period of time across portions of Thomas and Brooks counties, resulting in flash flooding of roads.
episodes.213585: Cluster of early morning showers offshore southwest Florida produced a waterspout west of North Captiva in Lee County.
episodes.213767: A grazing shortwave trough north of Utah sent a cold front into the region. Ahead of and along this boundary there was enough moisture to result in isolated to scattered convective development, with much of this activity higher based in nature. As a result, several strong to severe wind gusts were recorded or reported.
episodes.213951: A trough crossed Wyoming and brought scattered showers and thunderstorms. Very dry air at the low levels led to the showers and thunderstorms to be high based, and numerous locations saw dry microbursts as a result.
episodes.213967: The primary breakup front from the Upper Yukon tracked down through the middle section of the Yukon during the middle part of May. While some snowmelt flooding remained over parts of the Upper Yukon, primary dynamics shifted to significant mechanical ice jam releases, notably near the mouth of the Yuki River jam, which caused rapid surges downstream.
episodes.213974: Had extreme high wind verification from a thunderstorm outbreak as a system raced through Idaho.  Several power outages occurred with many recorded over 60 mph thunderstorm outflow wind gusts.
episodes.214049: High based thunderstorms developed ahead of an upper level trough around the Lordsburg Playa.  Due to the very dry air at the surface, wind gusts in excess of 75 mph developed and brought near zero visibilities to the area.
episodes.214473: A shortwave brought about windy thunderstorms across much of southern MT. In it's wake, a cold front crossed the area, and strong winds behind the front persisted well into the 14th. Non-convective gusts up to 80 mph were observed, with convective gusts up to 80 mph observed.

A severe thunderstorm crossed northern West Virginia through|Monongalia and Preston Counties on the afternoon of May 13th, 2026.|This storm produced wind damage and quarter size hail as it tracked|across the northern part of the state. Weak mid-level rotation|tightened and intensified as the storm reached western Preston|County and produced a brief tornado. The damage produced by this|storm, surveyed by UAS and security cameras, was determined to be tornadic and representative of an EF-0 with peak wind of 85 mph. Initial damage began along the west side of Moran Road, 3 miles east of  Reedsville, WV, where trees were uprooted and a roof was blown off a restaurant. This was deemed to be a surge of straight line wind damage. The character of the damage then became tornadic on the east side of Moran Road where several trees were uprooted, trunks of a few dead trees snapped, and large branches scattered within a wooded area. The tornado then continued through a few hundred yards of thick woods with sporadic tree damage noted before reaching Hovatter's Wildlife Zoo. Here, trees were snapped, uprooted, and large branches were scattered across the property. Security cameras on the property recorded a clear tornadic circulation, and visible convergence patterns in the |felled trees further confirmed the tornadic damage. The tornado then |dissipated on the east side of the zoo with no further distinguishable |path. The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh would like to thank Preston |County Emergency Management officials for their aerial footage and|aid with this survey.
